tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use windows-rs crate for Windows APIs with #[cfg(windows)] guards. For cross-platform, provide trait abstractions with platform-specific implementations. Registry access can use winreg crate. Process info via sysinfo crate (cross-platform).
tricky_patterns.notes: SharpHoundRPC is a major dependency containing Windows-only RPC/SMB/Registry/LSA APIs. Either port to Rust with FFI or use existing Rust Windows bindings.

locations: src/JsonExtensions.cs (CacheContractResolver uses reflection for property filtering)
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Replace reflection-based JSON serialization with explicit serde derives and custom serializers. Use serde field attributes for filtering.
tricky_patterns.notes: Avoid runtime reflection in Rust; use compile-time derives and macros

locations: Multiple locations with dynamic property access
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use strongly-typed enums or serde_json::Value for dynamic data. Prefer trait objects (Box<dyn Trait>) or enums over stringly-typed data.
tricky_patterns.notes: Rust's type system requires explicit handling; use serde's untagged enums or Value for truly dynamic data

tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use tokio as async runtime. async fn returns Result<T, E>. Task<T> → impl Future<Output = T> or explicit Future types. Use tokio::spawn for background tasks.
tricky_patterns.notes: Rust async is lower-level; requires explicit runtime. Use async_trait for trait methods.

tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use tokio::sync::mpsc for MPSC channels. Channel::CreateBounded(n) → mpsc::channel(n); Channel::CreateUnbounded() → mpsc::unbounded_channel(). Similar semantics.
tricky_patterns.notes: Nearly 1:1 mapping between .NET Channels and tokio mpsc

tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use ldap3 crate for LDAP protocol. Implement paged result controls manually (RFC 2696). Active Directory-specific queries require custom LDAP filter building. May need to port SharpHoundCommonLib LDAP utilities.
tricky_patterns.notes: LDAP is standardized but AD-specific features (e.g., Forest/Domain APIs, AdminSDHolder) require custom implementation

locations: Not used in SharpHound core (PowerShell wrapper uses reflection to call InvokeSharpHound)
tricky_patterns.mitigation: Not applicable for Rust port. PowerShell wrapper would use native library loading or separate CLI invocation.
tricky_patterns.notes: No equivalent needed; Rust doesn't have app domains

tricky_patterns.mitigation: Replace with Result<T, E> pattern. Use thiserror crate for custom error types with context. Implement std::error::Error trait. Use ? operator for propagation.
tricky_patterns.notes: Rust's Result type is more explicit; define error enums per module

tricky_patterns.mitigation: Implement Drop trait for cleanup. Use RAII pattern (resources in struct fields). tokio::fs handles are async Drop. Timers auto-cleanup when dropped.
tricky_patterns.notes: Rust's ownership makes cleanup automatic; explicit Drop for manual cleanup

tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use Option<T> for nullable types. String? → Option<String> or Option<&str>. Default values in clap use Option with default_value.
tricky_patterns.notes: Rust's Option is more explicit than C# nullability

tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use windows-rs crate: windows::Win32::Security::GetUserName or GetTokenInformation. Wrap in #[cfg(windows)]; provide fallback for Linux (getuid/geteuid).

Complex binary format parsing. Use windows-rs for SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR APIs on Windows. For cross-platform, implement SDDL parser or binary SD parser. Requires deep understanding of Windows security model.
tricky_patterns.notes: Critical for ACL collection; may require significant custom parsing code or FFI

tricky_patterns.mitigation: System.DirectoryServices.ActiveDirectory wraps complex LDAP queries. Must reimplement using raw LDAP queries to configuration/schema naming contexts. Requires LDAP knowledge of AD forest topology.
tricky_patterns.notes: No Rust equivalent; requires manual LDAP implementation

tricky_patterns.mitigation: Use DashMap crate (lock-free concurrent HashMap) or Arc<RwLock<HashMap>>. DashMap preferred for high-concurrency scenarios. RwLock for simple cases.
tricky_patterns.notes: DashMap provides similar performance to ConcurrentDictionary

risks_and_blockers.description: ~5000 LOC of core AD logic in external library. Contains all processor implementations (ACL, Group, Computer, etc.) and LDAP utilities.
risks_and_blockers.mitigation: Create separate 'sharphound-common' Rust crate. Port incrementally, starting with core types and LDAP utils. Use trait-based architecture for processors.

risks_and_blockers.description: ~3000 LOC of Windows RPC/SMB/Registry APIs. Windows-only functionality.
risks_and_blockers.mitigation: Create 'sharphound-rpc' crate using windows-rs FFI. Some APIs may require manual bindings. Consider phased approach: implement most critical RPCs first (NetSessionEnum, NetWkstaUserEnum), defer others.

risks_and_blockers.description: ldap3 crate may not support all AD-specific features (paged results, range retrieval, security descriptor parsing).
risks_and_blockers.mitigation: Implement custom LDAP controls as needed. AD schema knowledge required. Test against real domain controllers.

risks_and_blockers.description: Most functionality is Windows-centric. Linux support limited to LDAP queries only (no RPC/SMB).
risks_and_blockers.mitigation: Use #[cfg(windows)] guards extensively. Provide Linux-compatible subset (LDAP-only collection). Document platform limitations clearly.

risks_and_blockers.description: C# version uses 50 threads by default. Rust async may have different performance characteristics.
risks_and_blockers.mitigation: Use tokio with work-stealing scheduler. Benchmark against C# version. Tune thread pool and channel capacities. Likely to achieve equal or better performance.

risks_and_blockers.description: Many features require real Active Directory for proper testing.
risks_and_blockers.mitigation: Create mock LDAP server for unit tests. Use docker-based AD container for integration tests. Maintain test AD environment or use Azure AD DS for CI.

risks_and_blockers.description: Rust binaries with all dependencies may be larger than .NET merged exe.
risks_and_blockers.mitigation: Use release builds with LTO and strip. Consider UPX compression. Typical Rust binary: 5-15MB vs C# merged exe ~2-4MB. Acceptable tradeoff for no runtime dependency.
